Demonstrates various struct declarations, typedefs, and usage in C with print statements for verification.

# Purpose
The code demonstrates various ways to define and use structures in C. It includes examples of forward declarations, named and unnamed structures, typedefs, and global scope structures. The code also shows how to declare variables alongside struct definitions and how to use typedefs to simplify struct usage. The [`main`](<#main>) function initializes and manipulates these structures, demonstrating their usage and printing their values to verify correct operation.

Key components include the forward declaration of a struct (`struct ForwardDecl`), named structs with tags (`struct Named`), and typedefs for both named and unnamed structs (`MyStruct`, `MyAnonTypedef`). The code also includes a global unnamed struct (`global_data`) and a struct with an anonymous nested struct (`struct Outer`). The [`main`](<#main>) function serves as an executable entry point, showcasing the practical application of these struct definitions and typedefs by initializing variables, assigning values, and printing the results.
